4XpnKHJAok8.title: Tech Talk: Linus Torvalds on git
4XpnKHJAok8.summary: Linus Torvalds gives a Google tech talk on git, the source control system he created two years earlier. He argues for distributed version control over centralized systems such as CVS and Subversion.
4XpnKHJAok8.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the iconic explanation of why git is designed as it is and why distributed VCS beats centralized ones.

quote.text: This talk by Linus is iconic, if you haven't watched it you should.

p33CVV29OG8.title: Modern Dictionaries by Raymond Hettinger
p33CVV29OG8.summary: Python core developer Raymond Hettinger explains how Python's dictionary implementation evolved into the compact, ordered dict in Python 3.6. He uses pictures and small bits of pure Python, and covers key-sharing, compaction and versioning.
p33CVV29OG8.why: HN treats it as the definitive, engaging talk on hash table internals and Python dict ordering, and recommends it in tech-talk lists.

quote.text: one of the most insightful videos I've seen in a long time.

kPR8h4-qZdk.title: CppCon 2016: Nicholas Ormrod “The strange details of std::string at Facebook"
kPR8h4-qZdk.summary: Nicholas Ormrod's CppCon 2016 talk on how Facebook optimizes std::string with its open-source replacement fbstring. It covers storage layout tradeoffs, small string optimization and memory allocation behavior.
kPR8h4-qZdk.why: HN returns to it as the go-to talk on string internals, small string packing and why small percentage optimizations matter at scale.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: it's still definitely worth a watch

g6bOwQdCJrc.title: [CVPR'21 WAD] Keynote - Andrej Karpathy, Tesla
g6bOwQdCJrc.summary: Andrej Karpathy, then Tesla's head of AI, gives a CVPR 2021 workshop keynote on how Autopilot's neural networks work. A large part covers the move to a vision-only stack, including why radar was dropped and how vision produces depth estimates.
g6bOwQdCJrc.why: HN commenters cite it in Tesla threads as the primary-source explanation of why Tesla removed radar and how its vision depth estimation works.

quote.text: This talk was worth watching (any Karpathy or Carmack talk is imo)

3HxVMGaiZbc.title: ClojureScript in the Age of TypeScript — David Nolen
3HxVMGaiZbc.summary: David Nolen explains how ClojureScript is used at Vouch.io to build mobile and web software with a single language and REPL-driven workflow. The talk includes a live coding demo of React Native development.
3HxVMGaiZbc.why: Pointed to as a concrete demonstration of REPL-driven development and ClojureScript with React Native.

quote.text: David Nolen gave a relevant talk[0] about the workflow they use to integrate Clojure and React Native for mobile and web development

Z8ZhQPaw4rE.title: Solaris | SCIENCE FICTION | FULL MOVIE | directed by Tarkovsky
Z8ZhQPaw4rE.summary: Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 film Solaris, in which a psychologist is sent to a space station orbiting a planet with an alien intelligence and meets his dead wife there. It is the full movie, uploaded by Mosfilm.
Z8ZhQPaw4rE.why: HN recommends it as a masterpiece of emotional, contemplative science fiction, and draws analogies between its alien ocean and AI.

quote.text: the film's a masterpiece that I highly recommend

4KtotxNAwME.title: The Truth about Rust/WebAssembly Performance
4KtotxNAwME.summary: Leptos creator Greg Johnston examines Rust/WebAssembly frontend frameworks against JavaScript frameworks using the JS framework benchmark. He argues that WASM is no longer too slow for DOM-heavy rendering.
4KtotxNAwME.why: Cited as evidence that DOM access is not the bottleneck for WebAssembly, and as an explanation of signals-based updates versus virtual DOM.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: did a pretty good video about this a few weeks ago[0]

WrxZ4AZPdOQ.title: The Drive Home - ShaderToy
WrxZ4AZPdOQ.summary: A short ShaderToy piece by Martijn Steinrucken (The Art of Code) that renders rain on a windshield during a night drive, with blurred bokeh lights. It is set to music.
WrxZ4AZPdOQ.why: Shared as a stunning shader demo, with praise for its clear explanations of how it works.

quote.text: He does incredible work with shaders and explains them in very clear detail.

sf5OrthVRPA.title: Clutching at Random Straws, Matt Parker | LMS Popular Lectures 2010
sf5OrthVRPA.summary: Matt Parker's LMS popular lecture on how seemingly incredible results can be meaningless random patterns. He ranges from ancient Woolworths civilisations to shoelaces and DNA.
sf5OrthVRPA.why: Used to illustrate that humans pattern-match and find spurious patterns in enough data points.

quote.text: gave a very informative and entertaining lecture in 2010

uA0Z7_4J7u8.title: Succinct Data Structures
uA0Z7_4J7u8.summary: Edward Kmett's 2013 talk at Prezi in Budapest on succinct data structures, which store data in close to the information-theoretic minimum space while supporting fast queries. It ties together the research and walks through his Haskell succinct library.
uA0Z7_4J7u8.why: Commenters credit it as the place they first learned about succinct data structures, and found it left a lasting impression.

quote.text: one of his many talks that left me with an incredibly lasting impression

AqeJzItldSQ.title: Apollo Launch Abort System Test
AqeJzItldSQ.summary: Footage of an unmanned Apollo boilerplate capsule launched on a Little Joe II booster to test the launch escape system. The booster went out of control and broke up, but the escape system worked and the capsule was recovered undamaged.
AqeJzItldSQ.why: HN cites it as the classic example of a launch abort test that proved the design even though the rocket failed.

quote.text: the rocket accidentally broke apart but the escape tower system then performed perfectly

RQSBj2LKkWg.title: Userbenchmark - the April Fools that never ends
RQSBj2LKkWg.summary: 2kliksphilip examines UserBenchmark, a hardware comparison site known for strongly biased, pro-Intel writing. The video explains the site's credibility problems and points viewers to better sources for CPU and GPU information.
RQSBj2LKkWg.why: HN uses it as the go-to link to warn people not to trust UserBenchmark for hardware comparisons.

quote.text: There's a great video about the site here for those who are curious

V-vFtiDYiIw.title: Converting devices to USB Type-C
V-vFtiDYiIw.summary: DIY Perks shows how to modify devices that use older USB connectors so they charge and connect over USB Type-C. He solders in a USB-C connector board and works through cases such as dongle-dependent gadgets and a mouse receiver.
V-vFtiDYiIw.why: Commenters cite it as a well-made, practical example of USB-C conversion when they discuss hacking USB-C into devices.

quote.text: made a video about converting USB connectors to USB C which is very well done

YJg02ivYzSs.title: HYPER-REALITY
YJg02ivYzSs.summary: Keiichi Matsuda's short concept film depicting a future where physical and virtual realities have merged and the city is saturated with media and advertising. It shows an augmented-reality-filled daily life as a provocative vision.
YJg02ivYzSs.why: HN cites it as a shorthand for the dystopian risks of ad-driven, ubiquitous AR, usually in critical discussions of advertising and the metaverse.

quote.text: This is a great video that demonstrates some of the risks

62kxPyNZF3Q.title: other peoples money danny devito
62kxPyNZF3Q.summary: The shareholder speech by Larry the Liquidator, played by Danny DeVito, from the film Other People's Money. He argues that a dying company should be liquidated rather than kept alive.
62kxPyNZF3Q.why: Quoted in threads about declining companies and shrinking markets as a blunt statement of the case for liquidation.

quote.text: The best response to this is probably Larry the Liquidator's speech to shareholders

N5xfBtD6rLY.title: Military Recruitment and Hollywood
N5xfBtD6rLY.summary: Pop Culture Detective examines how the US military works with Hollywood, using the Independence Day sequel's Army recruitment tie-in as the starting point. It looks at the joint marketing between 20th Century Fox and the military.
N5xfBtD6rLY.sz: Pop Culture Detective 探讨美国军方与好莱坞的合作，以《独立日》续集的军队招募植入为切入点，分析 20th Century Fox 与军方的联合营销手段。
N5xfBtD6rLY.why: Cited in threads about military influence on movies and American cultural exports.
N5xfBtD6rLY.wz: 在讨论电影中的军方影响时，HN 常引用此片段。

quote.text: One of the resources the military provides is computer graphics assets like models of planes.

Xv2VIEY9-A8.title: Matt Foley: Van Down By The River - SNL
Xv2VIEY9-A8.summary: The classic SNL sketch in which motivational speaker Matt Foley, played by Chris Farley, warns teens they will end up living in a van down by the river.
Xv2VIEY9-A8.why: HN mostly drops it as a joke in threads about vans, van life or career failure.

YRyYIIFKsdU.title: The Eleventh HOPE (2016): Coding by Voice with Open Source Speech Recognition
YRyYIIFKsdU.summary: A HOPE XI talk on programming by voice with open source speech recognition. The speaker writes Linux systems code by voice and describes building custom voice grammars as an alternative to the keyboard for programmers with repetitive strain injuries.
YRyYIIFKsdU.why: HN cites it as proof that voice coding works and lists it among resources for programmers who can't type.

quote.text: Coding by Voice with Open Source Speech Recognition, from HOPE XI (2016)

_ogxZxu6cjM.title: Juking the Stats
_ogxZxu6cjM.summary: A short clip from The Wire in which police officers manipulate crime statistics to make the numbers look better. It dramatizes how metrics get gamed.
_ogxZxu6cjM.why: Used as a go-to illustration of Goodhart's law and statistical manipulation in institutions.

quote.text: Here is a clip that specifically shows Goodhart's law working in education.

ivrlU73VcHw.title: Windows 11 on Pentium 4
ivrlU73VcHw.summary: Enderman gets Windows 11 running on a Pentium 4 system with a Radeon HD 5870 and 8 GB of DDR2. It explores how an unsupported, ancient CPU can be made to work by using the rare last Pentium 4 variant and a registry flag.
ivrlU73VcHw.why: HN mentions it as a reference for Windows 11's actual CPU requirements and for how screen flicker is edited out of footage.

quote.text: he basically says that he needed to run the rare last variant of the Pentium IV to get it to work
